A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FEATHER study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, allowing reliable comparison of the methods, equations, experiments, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across 12 benchmarks, pruning-criteria and layer analyses, information-transfer controls, and comparisons against FastV and PyramidDrop.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds another encoder configuration, runtime measurements, additional baseline comparisons and a positional-embedding shuffling ablation.

M1.justification: FEATHER retains RoPE-free attention for token ranking, uniform sampling during pruning at layer 8, and further attention-based pruning at layer 16 with the same retention rule. The additional encoder experiment evaluates the existing method rather than revising its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 datasets covering localization, open-ended VQA and challenge tasks. The additional encoder and positional-shuffling experiments change model configurations and controls, without adding datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix A3 adds evaluated FasterVLM and VisionZip comparators, extending the comparison beyond the retained FastV and PyramidDrop approaches to pruning before the LLM. FasterVLM is adapted to SigLIP by averaging received attention instead of using CLS attention.

E3.justification: Appendices A1-A4 add evaluation with DINOv2+SigLIP, positional-embedding shuffling controls, and measured total runtime alongside theoretical FLOPs. The original main settings remain; explicitly excluding OCR tokens clarifies the existing TextVQA protocol rather than establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: The new shuffling ablation tests dependence on spatial position for both the unpruned model and FEATHER (Table A3). Table A1 also repeats the pruning-criteria analysis with DINOv2+SigLIP, testing whether the findings persist across encoders. Existing layer, criteria and information-transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 3.3 newly reports a chi-square test of selected tokens' vertical-position nonuniformity, with p-value below 0.05. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds or uncertainty intervals for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Existing localization values and headline comparisons are retained, with table fractions converted to percentages. v2 adds per-task criteria scores and new encoder, runtime, comparator and shuffling results. For example, Table A3 reports localization averages of 39.3 for FEATHER, 5.7 for FasterVLM and 8.5 for VisionZip at approximately comparable FLOPs reductions; shuffling reduces the unpruned model's average from 53.2 to 8.0.

T1.justification: The VLM and pruning formulations, FLOPs equation and density-distance definition are unchanged. The RoPE mechanism discussion is reorganized and expanded, but no mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims about positional bias in early pruning, benchmarks' limited assessment of fine-grained vision, and FEATHER's greater-than-fivefold localization improvement at comparable computational savings. The new contribution list explicitly summarizes findings already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explains differing TextVQA findings through OCR inputs, suggests lost positional information explains FasterVLM/VisionZip localization failures, and acknowledges that removing RoPE may unintentionally alter attention weights. These extend the retained positional-bias and benchmark-limitation interpretations.

D1.justification: New details specify OCR-free TextVQA inputs, the existing transfer-control experiment's two-pass implementation, once-per-pruning attention calculation and FlashAttention compatibility, NVIDIA L40S hardware, and FasterVLM's SigLIP adaptation. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on FasterVLM, VisionZip, ViT token reduction, FlashAttention and NaturalBench. Section 3.3 also contrasts its token-selection explanation with PyramidDrop's low-redundancy account, while retaining the paper's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, analysis sections and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. v2 adds an explicit contribution list, replaces boxed findings with integrated discussion and descriptive subheadings, relocates the RoPE explanation and ensemble definition, and reorganizes the supplement into Sections A1-A5.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially redesigned with individual task columns, grouped headings and delta rows. v2 adds Tables A1-A3 and runtime Figure A1, removes the boxed finding/insight displays, and enlarges one qualitative figure. Original Figures 6-8 are retained as Figures A2-A4.

improvement.justification: v1 supported efficiency primarily through theoretical FLOPs and evaluated one encoder setup with two principal acceleration baselines. v2 adds measured runtime, another encoder configuration, two additional baselines and a targeted positional-shuffling ablation. These address important empirical gaps and substantially strengthen the practical validation and support for the central diagnosis, while clearer presentation and explicit limitations improve assessability.
